column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “soul”; BSB interprets it as zeal.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew uses the image of breathing out lies; BSB says “utters.”
Hebrew retains the image of entreating a noble person’s face; BSB interprets seeking a prince’s favor.
The printed Hebrew has “to him they” after pursuing words; BSB says he pursues them with pleading but they cannot be found.
Hebrew says acquiring heart, loving one’s soul, and finding good; BSB has wisdom, himself, and success.
Hebrew uses the image of breathing out lies; BSB says “pours out.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew retains the image of lengthening anger and calls overlooking an offense his glory; BSB has patience and virtue.
Hebrew specifies a young lion; BSB has simply a lion.
Hebrew compares a wife’s quarrels to dripping; BSB makes the quarrelsome wife herself the subject.
Hebrew has singular “house”; BSB has plural houses.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “despises his ways”; BSB has being careless in them.
Hebrew makes the kind person the lender; BSB identifies kindness itself as the loan.
Hebrew says not to lift one’s soul toward killing him; BSB has not being party to his death.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “at your end”; BSB has “the rest of your days.”
Hebrew says “counsel”; BSB has “purpose.”
Hebrew expressly says “his” loving devotion and compares a poor man with a man of falsehood.
Hebrew describes lodging while satiated; BSB has resting content.
Hebrew presents burying the hand as completed; BSB uses present “buries.”
Hebrew says the simple man becomes prudent and the discerning understands knowledge; BSB has beware and gain knowledge.
Hebrew places the two actions together without BSB’s explicit “or.”
Hebrew directly commands “cease,” then has an infinitive “to stray”; BSB turns this into an if-clause and its predicted result.
Hebrew has “mouth of wicked people”; BSB has a wicked mouth.
Hebrew has singular “back” belonging to fools; BSB uses plural backs.
